Research suggests that hospital type can indeed affect the cost and outcomes of inpatient pediatric tonsillectomy. 

Children's hospitals and pediatric specialty hospitals tend to have better outcomes, such as lower complication rates and shorter lengths of stay, compared to general hospitals. However, the cost of care may be higher in these specialized hospitals due to their advanced equipment, specialized staff, and higher acuity of patients.

In contrast, general hospitals may have lower costs but potentially higher complication rates and longer lengths of stay. The difference in cost and outcomes may be attributed to the volume of procedures performed, the experience of the surgical team, and the availability of pediatric-specific resources and services.

Ultimately, the choice of hospital type for inpatient pediatric tonsillectomy should be based on individual patient needs, the severity of the condition, and the availability of specialized care. Families and healthcare providers should consider both the cost and quality of care when making decisions about where to receive treatment.
